items.html:
Request edit access to a project you can only view

You can now ask for edit access without leaving the project. Select Request to edit at the top of the project and add an optional message. Lovable emails the project's owner, or the workspace's admins and owners, who can approve or deny the request.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 17, 2026
items.summary: Request a higher workspace role Workspace viewers and editors can now request a higher role from the People tab. Viewers can ask for editor or admin access, and editors for admin access, each with an optional reason. You can withdraw a request while it is…
items.html:
Request a higher workspace role

Workspace viewers and editors can now request a higher role from the People tab. Viewers can ask for editor or admin access, and editors for admin access, each with an optional reason. You can withdraw a request while it is pending. Workspace admins and owners approve or deny it. Admin access requires a paid workspace plan.

Jump to your last chat in the desktop app

In the Lovable desktop app, tap Ctrl+Tab to switch to the chat you were in before. Hold Ctrl and press Tab to pick from your recent chats instead, with the chat you are in first. The shortcut uses Ctrl on macOS as well.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 16, 2026
items.summary: Require approval or block publishing with workspace policies Workspace admins and owners on Enterprise plans can now set workspace policies that block publishing or require an admin or owner to approve it first. Policies cover apps with unresolved findings of…
items.html:
Require approval or block publishing with workspace policies

Workspace admins and owners on Enterprise plans can now set workspace policies that block publishing or require an admin or owner to approve it first. Policies cover apps with unresolved findings of personal data, apps published by external collaborators, apps published publicly, apps that use connectors, and publishing from unverified email domains. When a policy requires approval, the person publishing sends a request from the publish dialog, and Lovable publishes the app when an admin or owner approves it. Enable policies in your workspace's Privacy & security settings.

Review publish requests and findings in the Action center

Workspace admins and owners on Business and Enterprise plans now have an Action center in the dashboard sidebar. It lists what needs a decision: publish requests waiting for approval, projects whose owner left the workspace, projects whose credit usage rose sharply, public apps with critical security findings, and public apps with no edits for months. From each row you can approve or deny a request, assign an owner, or unpublish an app.

Add OIDC sign-in to your app

In an app on the built-in backend (Cloud), you can now let your users sign in with your own OpenID Connect provider, such as Auth0, Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, or Keycloak, next to the other sign-in methods. Enable OIDC in your project's authentication settings and enter the details from your provider. Lovable then starts a build that adds the sign-in button to your app. The build is treated as standard build usage and consumes credits. Sign-ins consume no credits.

Lovable writes and runs tests for the rules you change

Lovable now adds a small test when you add or change a rule in your app, such as a price, a limit, or a permission. It runs the tests that cover the change before it reports the work as done, and keeps the tests in your project. Lovable does not write tests for copy, styling, or markup.

Connect your app to Pledge

You can now connect your Lovable app to Pledge to search verified nonprofits worldwide, create and track donations, and create and update fundraisers. It fits donation checkouts, loyalty point redemption, cause campaign pages, and employee giving programs. Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

GPT Transcribe for your app's speech-to-text features

Your app's AI features can now use OpenAI's GPT Transcribe (openai/gpt-transcribe), the new default speech-to-text model. It accepts audio files up to 25 MB, and your app can pass context, expected keywords, and languages as hints for names and specialist vocabulary. Ask Lovable to use it in your app, or describe what you want and let Lovable pick.

Formatted Markdown previews in the Files tab

Markdown files in your project's Files tab now open as formatted text, with tables, task lists, footnotes, and code blocks you can copy. Markdown files in Chats open in the same preview.

Larger document previews in the Files tab

A document you open in your project's Files tab now fills the preview pane. Its actions, such as adding it to the chat or a collection, are in the header above the document.

Removed: tabs in the desktop app

Tabs have been removed from the Lovable desktop app in version 1.9. The sidebar already lists your chats and projects, so the tabs were redundant. Switch between chats and projects from the sidebar, or hold Ctrl+Tab to pick from your recent chats. New downloads include 1.9, and the app offers the update when you open it.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 15, 2026
items.summary: Export audit logs to your SIEM or cloud storage Workspace admins and owners on Enterprise plans can now schedule exports of the workspace's audit logs to Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, Splunk, or Azure Log Analytics. Lovable delivers new…
items.html:
Export audit logs to your SIEM or cloud storage

Workspace admins and owners on Enterprise plans can now schedule exports of the workspace's audit logs to Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, Splunk, or Azure Log Analytics. Lovable delivers new events every hour or every 3 hours, so you can keep an audit trail for longer than the 13 weeks Lovable stores it and search Lovable activity next to your other security events. Find it under Workspace settings → Security → Data exports. Data exports come at no extra charge from Lovable. Your destination provider bills you for storage and ingestion.

Use Lovable from Claude through your company's SSO

Workspace admins and owners on Business and Enterprise plans can now enable enterprise-managed authentication, so members use the Lovable MCP server in Claude with their Okta identity, without a separate Lovable sign-in. Enable it in your workspace's Identity settings and pick the SSO provider your team already uses. Members keep their existing workspace and project permissions. Claude requires a Team or Enterprise plan.

Login pages include Sign in with Lovable by default

Login pages that Lovable builds for an app with Lovable Cloud now include Sign in with Lovable by default, alongside email and password sign-in and Google sign-in. Your app's users can sign in with their Lovable account, and Lovable registers the sign-in for your project with nothing to configure. To use a different set of methods, name them in your prompt. Sign-ins consume no credits.

GPT-6.1 Sol for your app's AI features

Your app's AI features can now use OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol (openai/gpt-6.1-sol), a model for complex coding and professional work. It accepts text and image input and responds with text. Ask Lovable to use it in your app, or describe what you want and let Lovable pick.

Documents in the project chat show their name and type

Documents that Lovable creates or refers to in a project chat reply now appear as a list with each file's name and a file-type icon, separate from the preview grid for images and videos. A single document with a preview, such as a PDF or a Markdown file, appears as a larger preview card. Select a row or card to open the file in the Files tab.

Select and sort files faster in the Files tab

In your project's Files tab, you can now select several files by hovering over a file and selecting its checkbox, then add them to the chat or a collection, download them, or delete them. Inside a collection, you can now sort files by Updated, Name, or Size, and the sort button shows which field is active. In list view, each document shows a file-type icon.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 14, 2026
items.summary: Growth tools: from building your app to growing it Lovable now helps you find customers, from the same chat where you build. Set a goal such as "my first 100 signups", and Growth tools turn it into a plan built from your app, your audience, and your traffic.…
items.html:
Growth tools: from building your app to growing it

Lovable now helps you find customers, from the same chat where you build. Set a goal such as "my first 100 signups", and Growth tools turn it into a plan built from your app, your audience, and your traffic. Lovable tells you what to fix first, and says so when ads are premature.

  • Growth advice that knows your app. Lovable recommends your next move: help search engines and AI assistants find your app, sharpen the offer on your landing page, prepare posts and listings for the communities, directories, and creators that reach your audience, or set up a Google Business Profile for a local business.
  • Ads launched from Lovable. Create a new Google Ads account or connect an existing one, and use your Facebook account for ads on Facebook and Instagram. Lovable sets up tracking and creates campaigns on Google, YouTube, Facebook, and Instagram. You decide the ad budget and approve when spending can start.
  • Creative built from your app. Ask for a launch video, an animated product demo, a video ad, images, or ad copy that match your brand, ready for a campaign, a social post, or customer outreach.

Results show in the redesigned Analytics view: visits by channel, campaign results on the Ads tab, and a Get more visitors button that sends your current traffic to Lovable with your request. Lovable adds no extra fees for using Growth tools, and the standard costs of chatting with Lovable apply. Google or Meta charges the payment method on your advertising account for the ads you run.

Add Sign in with Lovable to any website

You can now let people sign in to your website with their Lovable account, including a site you did not build with Lovable. Add one script tag and a button, and your site receives the person's name, email address, and picture, depending on which of those you ask for. If your site has a server, you can use the standard OpenID Connect flow in place of the script. Both paths start from an OAuth client registered in your workspace settings. Sign-ins consume no credits.

Connect your apps to Lovable with OAuth

Workspace admins and owners can now register OAuth clients under Workspace settings → API keys & OAuth → OAuth clients. An OAuth client lets your app ask each user to allow access to their profile, projects, or workspaces, and gives you a client ID and, for a Web server client, a client secret. Sensitive scopes, which read or change projects and workspaces, require a Business or Enterprise plan and verification from Lovable. Users see a warning until the client is verified.

Let your app's users sign in with their Lovable account

In an app with Lovable Cloud, you can now let your users sign in with their Lovable account. Enable it in your project's auth settings, or ask Lovable in the project chat to add the button. Lovable registers the sign-in for your project and keeps it current when your app's address changes. Your app receives each user's name, email address, and profile picture, and the consent screen shows your project's name. Sign-ins consume no credits.

Ask Lovable what drives your run credit usage

You can now ask Lovable what drives run credit usage in the project chat. Lovable reads the recorded usage, investigates the app's scheduled jobs, functions, database, storage, and AI activity, traces what it finds to the project's code, and proposes fixes. Lovable makes a change only when you ask for it. Workspace admins and owners can also ask in Chats which projects and usage categories drive the whole workspace's run credit usage.

From the usage chart, workspace admins and owners can start the same investigation with Optimize your usage. The button appears below the chart in Usage details and in a project's Cloud usage view when the workspace or project used more than 5 run credits in the last 7 days. In Usage details, it starts a workspace-wide investigation in Chats. In a project, it starts the investigation in the project chat, in Chat mode, where Lovable does not edit your project's code.

Connect your app to Bing Webmaster Tools

You can now connect your Lovable app to Bing Webmaster Tools to read clicks, impressions, top queries, and crawl stats for the sites verified in your Bing Webmaster Tools account, and to submit URLs and sitemaps. It fits search dashboards, crawl monitors, and tools that send new pages or feeds to Bing. Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Restore a deleted project yourself

You can now restore a deleted project for 60 days after you delete it. Select Restore under Recently deleted projects in your workspace settings. The project returns with its code, version history, and chat history, and a paused Cloud backend resumes. You can restore the projects you own. Workspace owners can restore every deleted project in the workspace, whoever deleted it. After 60 days, the project is permanently deleted.

Restore a deleted workspace yourself

Workspace owners on Free, Pro, and Business plans can now restore a deleted workspace, with its projects and members, for 60 days after deleting it. Select Restore under Recently deleted workspaces in your account settings. If the workspace's subscription ended while it was deleted, the workspace returns on the Free plan. After 60 days, the workspace is permanently deleted.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 13, 2026
items.summary: Let browser agents use your app You can now let browser agents use your app. When you enable agent integrations, Lovable also adds WebMCP tools to your app, so an AI agent built into the browser can act on the page a person has open, such as marking a task as…
items.html:
Let browser agents use your app

You can now let browser agents use your app. When you enable agent integrations, Lovable also adds WebMCP tools to your app, so an AI agent built into the browser can act on the page a person has open, such as marking a task as done or filtering a list. Browser tools run in the person's own browser tab with their signed-in session, separate from your app's MCP server, and you can also ask Lovable in the project chat to add them without a server. Lovable starts with tools that read information or are easy to undo, and adds tools that delete, pay, send, publish, or share only when you ask.

Gemini 4 Argon for your app's AI features

Your app's AI features can now use Google's Gemini 4 Argon (google/gemini-4-argon), a frontier model for long-horizon coding, reasoning, and knowledge work. It accepts text, image, audio, and video input and comes at a premium price. Ask Lovable to use it in your app, or describe what you want and let Lovable pick.

Approve every tool from a chat connector at once

You can now select Always allow all tools from this connection when Lovable asks you to approve a tool from a chat connector, and every tool from that connection runs without asking from then on, including tools the server adds later. The choice applies to your own approvals only, and you can change it in the connection's settings in Connectors.

Supported PostgreSQL extensions on Lovable Cloud

Lovable Cloud databases support a fixed set of PostgreSQL extensions, such as pg_cron, pg_net, vector, and postgis. Lovable now refuses CREATE EXTENSION for any other extension, in the project chat, the SQL editor, and the Lovable API, and builds the feature with plain SQL instead. Extensions already installed in your database keep working.

Search for individual settings

You can now search for individual settings in workspace settings. Start typing in the search box at the top of the settings sidebar, and the results list the matching settings grouped by settings page, with the matching words highlighted. Select a result to open that setting.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 12, 2026
items.summary: Edit images directly in the Files tab You can now mark a change directly on an image in your project's Files tab. Open the image and select Edit, then draw over an area and describe the change, pin a comment where you want something changed, erase what you…
items.html:
Edit images directly in the Files tab

You can now mark a change directly on an image in your project's Files tab. Open the image and select Edit, then draw over an area and describe the change, pin a comment where you want something changed, erase what you want removed, or remove the background. Lovable saves the result as a new file next to the original.

See how much usage your free allowances cover

On Free, Pro, and Business plans, you can now see how much of your usage the free allowances covered. Usage details shows the covered credits next to the total above the chart, and the By coverage view splits each bar into what the daily build credits, the daily chat allowance, and the monthly Cloud, AI, and connector grants paid for, and what drew on your general credits.

Connect your app to Loops

You can now connect your Lovable app to Loops to create and update contacts, send events that start your Loops automations, and send transactional email you manage in Loops. It fits waitlists, signup forms, and product notifications that should reach people from your Loops audience. Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 9, 2026
items.summary: Publish every app in your workspace under your own domain Workspace admins and owners on Enterprise plans can now set a publishing domain for the workspace, so projects publish at your-app.yourdomain.com instead of your-app.lovable.app. Pick a domain you…
items.html:
Publish every app in your workspace under your own domain

Workspace admins and owners on Enterprise plans can now set a publishing domain for the workspace, so projects publish at your-app.yourdomain.com instead of your-app.lovable.app. Pick a domain you bought through Lovable, or a subdomain of it, with no DNS setup. You can also connect a domain or subdomain you own elsewhere. Each project moves to the new address the next time you publish it, and its existing lovable.app address keeps working. Find it under Workspace settings → Workspace domains → Publishing domain.

Reference another chat or send it a task

In Chats, you can now work with your other chats. Reference a chat to let Lovable read what you discussed there, or ask Lovable to send a message to another chat or to start a new chat with a first task. Type @ and select the chat under Chats, or paste a link to the chat. The other chat does the work and can reply in your conversation, so one chat can coordinate several others.

Generate a secret that another app also needs

When Lovable asks you for a secret that you enter in two places, such as the secret GitHub uses to sign its webhook requests or a token two of your apps share, the secret form now has a Generate button. Select it to fill in a strong random value, copy the value to the other place, and submit. Lovable shows the value only in the form, and does not repeat stored secret values, or anything derived from them, in the project chat, in logs, or in your code.

Buy .si domains through Lovable

You can now buy .si domains, the Slovenian country-code extension, through Lovable. Search for the full name including the extension from Buy a domain in your project's or workspace's domain settings. A new .si domain can take up to 2 hours to start working, and you can register it for up to 5 years.

Get a warning before your credits run out

On Free, Pro, and Business plans, workspace admins and owners now get a warning when the workspace is likely to run out of credits before its monthly credits refill. The warning appears on the Plans & credit usage page and in Usage details, shows when your credits are expected to run out and when your monthly credits refill, and lets you add credits before your published apps are affected.

Enterprise credit balances now appear as numbers

On Enterprise plans, the credit panel on the Plans & credit usage page now shows your balance as numbers in place of a progress bar. Admins and owners see how many workspace credits remain and the workspace total, for example 6,400 remaining of 10,000. When the workspace has used more than its commitment, they also see a warning and an Overage credits row. Other members see only their own personal credits.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 8, 2026
items.summary: Publish to invited people only on Free and Pro plans On Free and Pro plans, you can now publish your app to an invite-only audience. In the publish dialog, select Invite only, then add workspace members by name or invite people outside your workspace by email.…
items.html:
Publish to invited people only on Free and Pro plans

On Free and Pro plans, you can now publish your app to an invite-only audience. In the publish dialog, select Invite only, then add workspace members by name or invite people outside your workspace by email. Only the people you add can visit the published app, after logging in, along with the project owner, workspace owners, and people the project is shared with directly. Publishing to your whole workspace or to groups still requires a Business or Enterprise plan.

App + chat connectors: Zendesk, Neon, MotherDuck, Oracle Autonomous AI Database, IBM Db2, Qlik Cloud, Omni, Metabase, and GoodData

Nine new app + chat connectors let your apps work with your help desk, your own databases, and the metrics your team defines in a business intelligence tool. Add them from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect one.

  • Manage Zendesk support tickets from your app. Zendesk lets apps read, create, and update support tickets, look up users and organizations, and read help center articles.
  • Query your own database from your app:
    • Neon lets apps read and write your own Neon Postgres database with SQL.
    • MotherDuck lets apps run DuckDB SQL on your MotherDuck databases and shares.
    • Oracle Autonomous AI Database lets apps run SQL on your Oracle Autonomous AI Database, including the Oracle Fusion ERP and HCM data that Fusion Data Intelligence stores there.
    • IBM Db2 lets apps run SQL on Db2 on Cloud.
  • Show your team's BI metrics in your app:
    • Qlik Cloud lets apps browse your Qlik apps, export chart and table data, ask Insight Advisor questions, and start reloads.
    • Omni lets apps query the topics and measures your team defines in Omni and draw their own charts from the results.
    • Metabase lets apps run saved Metabase questions and custom queries against the databases connected to Metabase, on Metabase Cloud or a self-hosted instance.
    • GoodData lets apps read the workspaces, metrics, and saved visualizations in GoodData Cloud and compute reports from them.
Chat connectors: Loom

Loom is now available as a prebuilt chat connector, so Lovable can read a Loom video's transcript, AI summary, and comments while you build. Paste a Loom link in the project chat to show Lovable a bug or an idea instead of describing it. Add it from Connectors.

Removed: design directions before the first build

The three design directions Lovable showed before building a visually open-ended prompt have been removed. Lovable now builds the look directly from what you describe, and still asks design questions about color, typography, and layout when your prompt leaves the look open. Older chats keep the direction you picked, without the previews.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 7, 2026
items.summary: Set credit usage limits and alerts for your workspace Workspace admins and owners on paid plans can now set usage limits and alerts that keep shared credits under control. Set a credit threshold for the whole workspace, a project, a member, or, on Business and…
items.html:
Set credit usage limits and alerts for your workspace

Workspace admins and owners on paid plans can now set usage limits and alerts that keep shared credits under control. Set a credit threshold for the whole workspace, a project, a member, or, on Business and Enterprise plans, a group or an access token, and choose what happens when usage reaches it: an email or in-app alert, or a block that stops building or pauses Lovable Cloud, AI features, and metered connector requests in deployed apps. You can also get an alert when your workspace balance drops below an amount or percentage you choose, and members who reach a blocking limit can request an increase that you approve or deny. Find it under Workspace settings → Usage limits & alerts.

Get help when your Cloud database is under high load

When your Lovable Cloud database runs low on resources, Lovable can now warn you that your app is under high load in the project chat, in the Publish dialog, and in More → Cloud → Database. Click Resolve to have Lovable check whether the database is still under pressure, find the likely cause, and suggest query or code changes before you move to a larger instance. When a larger instance is the right fix, Lovable shows the credit impact and offers the resize for your approval. Resizing from chat is available on paid plans.

Cloud database changes are now recorded as Drizzle migrations

When Lovable changes the structure of your Lovable Cloud database, it now records each change as a migration file in your project's code, under drizzle/migrations/. Lovable uses Drizzle, an open-source tool for database migrations, to create and apply these files. A migration file is a SQL file that describes one change to the database structure, so your code carries the full history of how your database was built. Lovable also refuses changes that could break your published app, such as dropping or renaming a table or column, and reaches the same result by adding to your database instead, for example by adding a new column and copying the data over. To let Lovable make such changes directly, set Execute backward incompatible database migrations in your Cloud permissions.

Faster inline text edits

Simple text changes you make with Edit text inline in the preview toolbar now apply in a few seconds. Text that your app builds from data or translates still takes a little longer.

Gemini 3.7 Flash is deprecated for your app's AI features

Google is retiring Gemini 3.7 Flash (google/gemini-3.7-flash), so it is now marked deprecated for your app's AI features and stops working on January 28, 2027. Apps that use it keep working until then, and Lovable no longer picks it for new AI features. If your app uses it, ask Lovable to switch to Gemini 3.8 Flash (google/gemini-3.8-flash) before that date.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 6, 2026
items.summary: Connect your app to Klaviyo You can now connect your Lovable app to Klaviyo to look up and update customer profiles, subscribe people to a list when they give email or SMS consent, record events such as signups and purchases, and read your campaigns and flows.…
items.html:
Connect your app to Klaviyo

You can now connect your Lovable app to Klaviyo to look up and update customer profiles, subscribe people to a list when they give email or SMS consent, record events such as signups and purchases, and read your campaigns and flows. It fits newsletter signup forms, SMS opt-in forms, and internal pages that show campaign status. Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Chat connectors: Excalidraw+

Excalidraw+ is now available as a prebuilt chat connector, so Lovable can list, search, and edit the scenes in your Excalidraw+ workspace while you build, including diagrams, wireframes, and presentations. Add it from Connectors.

Connect to Databricks with your own account

The Databricks connector now lets you connect by signing in with your own Databricks account instead of a service principal. Select User OAuth when you create the connection. Queries run as you, so your own Unity Catalog permissions apply and Databricks audit logs show who ran each query.

Redesigned model list for the built-in AI connector

The AI connector in Connectors now lists every model your app's AI features can use as a card with its name, provider, a short description, and what it does. Search the list by model name, provider, or capability.

Gemini 3.6 Flash is deprecated for your app's AI features

Google is retiring Gemini 3.6 Flash (google/gemini-3.6-flash), so it is now marked deprecated for your app's AI features and stops working on November 19, 2026. Apps that use it keep working until then, and Lovable no longer picks it for new AI features. If your app uses it, ask Lovable to switch to Gemini 3.8 Flash (google/gemini-3.8-flash) before that date.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 5, 2026
items.summary: Lyria 3 music models for your app's AI features Your app's AI features can now generate music with two Google models, from a text prompt or an image, with vocals or as an instrumental: Lyria 3 Clip Preview, for clips of about 30 seconds. Lyria 3 Pro Preview,…
items.html:
Lyria 3 music models for your app's AI features

Your app's AI features can now generate music with two Google models, from a text prompt or an image, with vocals or as an instrumental:

  • Lyria 3 Clip Preview, for clips of about 30 seconds.
  • Lyria 3 Pro Preview, for full tracks up to 184 seconds.

Ask Lovable to use either model in your app, or describe what you want and let Lovable pick. Generating music uses credits, charged per finished track and only when a generation succeeds.

App + chat connectors: beehiiv and Ramp

beehiiv lets apps add subscribers, show posts from your publication, and save draft posts. Use it for signup forms, post listings, and launch waitlists for a newsletter you already run.

Ramp lets apps read the transactions, cards, funds and spending limits, users, and business information of your Ramp business. Use it for spend dashboards, transaction reporting, and card and limit inventories.

Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Restore Lovable work after a push to your Git repository replaces it

You can now restore work Lovable made after a push to your synced repository replaces it. Lovable saves a backup first and shows a notice in the editor and in Project settings → Git, where the project owner restores the saved work or keeps the repository's version. Restored work syncs back to your repository, or to a lovable-sync branch when the repository has newer commits.

items.title: ECA 0.166.0
items.summary: Fix resuming a chat restoring the default agent instead of the chat's own agent when it was picked before the first message. #657 Fix the "dropped N history entries from a previous provider" note repeating on every prompt after a model swap; it now shows once…
items.html:
• Fix resuming a chat restoring the default agent instead of the chat's own agent when it was picked before the first message. #657
  • Fix the "dropped N history entries from a previous provider" note repeating on every prompt after a model swap; it now shows once per swap. #660
  • Fix install script exiting silently when unzip is missing; report missing tools and download errors clearly, and keep the existing binary on failure. #655
  • Fix context-overflow auto-recovery not triggering for llama.cpp's llama-server, whose "exceeds the available context size" error went unrecognized.
  • Speed up rollback, flags and forks on long chats via the incrementalUpdates capability: chat/truncated, positioned flags, and paged /fork, /btw and chat/fork.
  • grep no longer reports no matches as a failed tool call; backend errors still fail with the backend message.

items.title: ECA 0.165.1
items.summary: Add toolCall.askUser.trustModeTimeoutSeconds: in trust mode, an unanswered ask_user question times out and the LLM continues with its best judgment. Fix OpenAI-compatible chat splitting text around a duplicate thinking block, or dropping a few characters, when…
items.html:
• Add toolCall.askUser.trustModeTimeoutSeconds: in trust mode, an unanswered ask_user question times out and the LLM continues with its best judgment.
  • Fix OpenAI-compatible chat splitting text around a duplicate thinking block, or dropping a few characters, when one stream chunk carries both reasoning and text.

items.title: ECA 0.165.0
items.summary: Fix "Waiting for tool call approval" progress being replaced by "Generating" when another tool call finishes while one still waits for approval. eca-emacs#334 Retry or auto-continue Anthropic streams that fail mid-response with an api_error, overloaded_error…
items.html:
• Fix "Waiting for tool call approval" progress being replaced by "Generating" when another tool call finishes while one still waits for approval. eca-emacs#334
  • Retry or auto-continue Anthropic streams that fail mid-response with an api_error, overloaded_error or timeout_error SSE event, instead of ending the prompt.
  • Refill the maxAutoContinues recovery budget once a response completes and its tools run, so long turns aren't stopped by failures spread across many steps.
  • Show consecutive thinking blocks as a single block in chat, live and on resume, without changing the history sent to providers. #643
  • Show subscription quota (Claude Pro/Max, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot) with reset times instead of costs in chat usage and provider status, plus a /quota command. #641

items.title: ECA 0.164.0
items.summary: Fix "Waiting for tool call approval" progress being replaced by "Generating" when another tool call finishes while one still waits for approval. eca-emacs#334 Scope "approve & remember" approvals to the chat and its subagents instead of all chats, add…
items.html:
• Fix "Waiting for tool call approval" progress being replaced by "Generating" when another tool call finishes while one still waits for approval. eca-emacs#334
  • Scope "approve & remember" approvals to the chat and its subagents instead of all chats, add /approvals and /forget-approvals commands to list and forget them. #639

items.title: ECA 0.163.1
items.summary: Stop the shell_command prompt from asking for a description of the command, as the tool has no such param and calls with it now fail.
items.html: • Stop the shell_command prompt from asking for a description of the command, as the tool has no such param and calls with it now fail.

items.title: ECA 0.163.0
items.summary: Add subagent timeoutSeconds; on timeout or max steps the subagent gets a final no-tools turn to report findings, and a parent stop keeps its partial output. #625 Fix tool-call continuations sending the provider key resolved at prompt start, so a ${cmd:...} key…
items.html:
• Add subagent timeoutSeconds; on timeout or max steps the subagent gets a final no-tools turn to report findings, and a parent stop keeps its partial output. #625
  • Fix tool-call continuations sending the provider key resolved at prompt start, so a ${cmd:...} key that prints a short-lived token no longer expires mid-prompt; continuations read the key from the current config. #634
  • Support multiple accounts of the same provider (e.g. work and personal subscriptions) via provider inherit, like "anthropic-work": {"inherit": "anthropic"}. #617
  • Fix ECA processes overwriting each other's refreshed provider logins in the global cache.

items.title: ECA 0.161.2
items.summary: List the new OpenAI gpt-6-sol/gpt-6-luna models for ChatGPT OAuth accounts by bumping the Codex client version the backend gates on. Fix /agent, /model and remote UI agent changes being reverted by the editor's next prompt; /resume now also restores the chat…
items.html:
• List the new OpenAI gpt-6-sol/gpt-6-luna models for ChatGPT OAuth accounts by bumping the Codex client version the backend gates on.
  • Fix /agent, /model and remote UI agent changes being reverted by the editor's next prompt; /resume now also restores the chat agent. eca-emacs#327
  • Retry transient openai-chat post-tool failures (e.g. 502) before new output without rerunning tools, so sub-agents survive flaky gateways. #620

items.title: ECA 0.161.1
items.summary: Add Claude Opus 5.5 support.
items.html: • Add Claude Opus 5.5 support.

items.title: ECA 0.161.0
items.summary: Pin plugin sources to verified commits, add explicit /plugin-update, and preserve marketplace identity when installing plugins. Retry transient Anthropic post-tool failures before new output without rerunning tools; show recovery counts and explain exhausted…
items.html:
• Pin plugin sources to verified commits, add explicit /plugin-update, and preserve marketplace identity when installing plugins.
  • Retry transient Anthropic post-tool failures before new output without rerunning tools; show recovery counts and explain exhausted or disabled recovery.
  • Expand @file references in custom-command and parameterized-skill arguments into file content before sending the prompt. #163
  • Fix steered native commands (e.g. /sync-system-prompt) being sent to the LLM as text while the chat runs: run them at the next turn boundary or refuse chat-changing ones. #610
  • Return globalConfigPath in the initialize response so clients open the config file the server actually reads.

items.title: ECA 0.160.3
items.summary: Fix built-in GPT-5.x/GPT-6 variants on openai-chat providers (e.g. LiteLLM/Azure gateways) sending the Responses reasoning object (Unknown parameter: 'reasoning'); they now send reasoning_effort. #609
items.html: • Fix built-in GPT-5.x/GPT-6 variants on openai-chat providers (e.g. LiteLLM/Azure gateways) sending the Responses reasoning object (Unknown parameter: 'reasoning'); they now send reasoning_effort. #609

items.title: ECA 0.160.2
items.summary: Retry one transient GitHub Copilot token-renewal gateway/service failure. #551 Build native binaries with GraalVM for JDK 25: fixes the idle server burning one CPU core per HTTPS connection closed by a gateway mid-stream. #608
items.html:
• Retry one transient GitHub Copilot token-renewal gateway/service failure. #551
  • Build native binaries with GraalVM for JDK 25: fixes the idle server burning one CPU core per HTTPS connection closed by a gateway mid-stream. #608

items.title: ECA 0.160.1
items.summary: Fix answering pending questions from the remote UI without SSE subscribers; the first editor or HTTP answer wins. Fix GitHub Copilot gpt-5.6-*/gpt-6-* models sent to Chat Completions (unsupported_api_for_model) when the /models catalog is unavailable: gpt >=…
items.html:
• Fix answering pending questions from the remote UI without SSE subscribers; the first editor or HTTP answer wins.
  • Fix GitHub Copilot gpt-5.6-*/gpt-6-* models sent to Chat Completions (unsupported_api_for_model) when the /models catalog is unavailable: gpt >= 5.3 route to Responses by name.
  • Keep the catalog API and reasoning variants of hidden GitHub Copilot models (e.g. disabled policy) that are listed explicitly under the provider models config.

items.title: ECA 0.160.0
items.summary: Fix context usage counting only output tokens on anthropic-compatible providers that report input usage in message_delta (e.g. Z.AI). #604 Accept unescaped square brackets, non-ASCII and other reserved chars in workspace file URI paths. #594 #605 Fix inflated…
items.html:
• Fix context usage counting only output tokens on anthropic-compatible providers that report input usage in message_delta (e.g. Z.AI). #604
  • Accept unescaped square brackets, non-ASCII and other reserved chars in workspace file URI paths. #594 #605
  • Fix inflated costs for OpenAI-compatible providers (e.g. Synthetic); count usage once per request before completion and retain received usage on stream errors.
  • Tool prompts: push, git config, shell search/read and sub-agents run on explicit request; rule headings are tool-scoped.
  • Recover Anthropic streaming responses interrupted by transient TLS bad_record_mac failures.
  • BREAKING: plugins.install now appends across config layers. Set plugins.installMode to replace beside the list to exclude inherited plugins as before.
  • Add mcpToolSearch config to keep MCP tool schemas out of context until the LLM loads them with the new eca__search_tools tool.
  • Fix /compact steered while the chat is running: compact with its instructions at the next turn boundary and resume the task, instead of sending it to the LLM as text. #600
  • Hide GitHub Copilot models the account can't use (model_picker_enabled: false or a disabled policy) instead of listing the whole catalog, and don't fall back to models.dev when none is usable. #601
  • Pick the GitHub Copilot default model from the account's catalog (versatile, then powerful, then lightweight category) instead of hardcoding gpt-5.5, which some plans don't include.
  • Fix remote MCP servers whose SSE events omit the space after event: (e.g. Z.AI) hanging on initialize; bump plumcp to 0.2.3. #586

items.title: ECA 0.159.0
items.summary: Fix spawn_agent details to include the agent's configured variant; it was only sent when the LLM passed the variant argument explicitly. Add gpt-6-astra support: built-in variants low, medium, high, xhigh, max (no none), Codex Lite/context fallbacks, web…
items.html:
• Fix spawn_agent details to include the agent's configured variant; it was only sent when the LLM passed the variant argument explicitly.
  • Add gpt-6-astra support: built-in variants low, medium, high, xhigh, max (no none), Codex Lite/context fallbacks, web search and image generation.
  • Fix directory_tree hiding gitignored files but not their directories (e.g. .git, target); listing an ignored dir directly now shows its contents.
  • Honor no_proxy/NO_PROXY when routing HTTP and HTTPS requests through environment-configured proxies. #583
  • Stop retrying provider 429 errors that report exhausted usage or billing quota. #405
  • Add /agent to switch a chat's primary agent without resetting its established model or variant. #428
  • Add autoCompactTokensLeft to auto-compact when a fixed number of context tokens remain instead of a percentage. #582
  • Add view_image tool so the agent can load png/jpg/gif/webp files from disk into context as images for models with image input.

items.title: ECA 0.158.1
items.summary: Echo user prompt and show a "Loading config" progress before resolving config, so slow ${cmd:...} keys no longer delay the chat UI. Fix config cache thrashing on unrelated db changes, which re-ran ${cmd:...} commands on every request and poll; cache successful…
items.html:
• Echo user prompt and show a "Loading config" progress before resolving config, so slow ${cmd:...} keys no longer delay the chat UI.
  • Fix config cache thrashing on unrelated db changes, which re-ran ${cmd:...} commands on every request and poll; cache successful ${cmd:...} results for 5 minutes.

items.title: ECA 0.158.0
items.summary: Build fallback variants from /v1/models advertised reasoning efforts (OpenRouter, Synthetic) when no built-in or user variants exist. Add /chats command listing chats from all workspaces grouped by workspace path, with optional title filter. Workspace roots…
items.html:
• Build fallback variants from /v1/models advertised reasoning efforts (OpenRouter, Synthetic) when no built-in or user variants exist.
  • Add /chats command listing chats from all workspaces grouped by workspace path, with optional title filter. Workspace roots are persisted in the chats index or hash-recovered.
  • Add Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 support.

items.title: ECA 0.157.3
items.summary: Add built-in effort variants for Claude models on openai-chat providers like OpenRouter, using the verbosity param which maps to Anthropic's output_config.effort.
items.html: • Add built-in effort variants for Claude models on openai-chat providers like OpenRouter, using the verbosity param which maps to Anthropic's output_config.effort.

items.html: • Set ECA_AGENT=1 and ECA_CHAT_ID env vars on commands spawned by shell, git, custom tools and hooks so external tooling can detect ECA-spawned commands.

items.html:
• Add chat/inlinePrompt protocol method: inline editor prompts backed by regular chats, optionally forking an existing chat without replay. New chatInline config for model/agent/variant defaults.
  • Return the new chatId in the chat/fork response and tag inline chats with kind in chat/list.

items.title: ECA 0.156.0
items.summary: Add /btw command to ask a side question in a forked chat, keeping the current chat history clean. Runs immediately even while the chat is running (steered /btw is not queued). Add /delete-chat command to permanently delete the current chat or a chat-id from…
items.html:
• Add /btw command to ask a side question in a forked chat, keeping the current chat history clean. Runs immediately even while the chat is running (steered /btw is not queued).
  • Add /delete-chat command to permanently delete the current chat or a chat-id from the /resume list, asking confirmation first.

items.title: ECA 0.155.2
items.summary: Discover model context limit from llama.cpp/llama-swap /models meta.n_ctx/n_ctx_train, enabling usage limit and auto-compaction for local providers. #577 Restore parallel function-call batching for ChatGPT OAuth models that advertise Responses Lite and…
items.html:
• Discover model context limit from llama.cpp/llama-swap /models meta.n_ctx/n_ctx_train, enabling usage limit and auto-compaction for local providers. #577
  • Restore parallel function-call batching for ChatGPT OAuth models that advertise Responses Lite and parallel tool-call support. #572
  • Increase chatRetentionDays from 14 -> 30.

items.title: ECA 0.155.1
items.summary: Fix Anthropic streaming dropping tool calls when providers report end_turn/stop stop_reason with pending tool_use blocks. #576
items.html: • Fix Anthropic streaming dropping tool calls when providers report end_turn/stop stop_reason with pending tool_use blocks. #576

items.html: • Add editor_definition and editor_references tools backed by the editor's language server, behind new client capabilities and toolCall.editorNav.enabled config. #351

items.title: ECA 0.154.2
items.summary: Retry LLM requests on network failures (VPN/wifi drops: DNS, refused or timed-out connects) with "Network issues" progress, instead of failing or hanging. Add connectTimeoutSeconds config (default 15) so requests fail fast instead of hanging when the network…
items.html:
• Retry LLM requests on network failures (VPN/wifi drops: DNS, refused or timed-out connects) with "Network issues" progress, instead of failing or hanging.
  • Add connectTimeoutSeconds config (default 15) so requests fail fast instead of hanging when the network black-holes connections.

items.title: ECA 0.154.1
items.summary: Skip redundant MCP tool/serverUpdated notification after prompts/resources listing when the server has none. Chat retention (chatRetentionDays) now considers when the chat was last updated instead of when it was created, keeping old but still active chats.
items.html:
• Skip redundant MCP tool/serverUpdated notification after prompts/resources listing when the server has none.
  • Chat retention (chatRetentionDays) now considers when the chat was last updated instead of when it was created, keeping old but still active chats.

items.title: ECA 0.154.0
items.summary: Improve /login UX: markdown links, provider/method selection via chat/askQuestion when supported by client, GitHub Copilot login completes automatically, secrets not echoed. Mark MCP servers as running right after tools listing, fetching prompts/resources…
items.html:
• Improve /login UX: markdown links, provider/method selection via chat/askQuestion when supported by client, GitHub Copilot login completes automatically, secrets not echoed.
  • Mark MCP servers as running right after tools listing, fetching prompts/resources afterwards so slow/unresponsive list requests don't delay server startup.
  • Ask user consent and enable the GitHub Copilot per-model policy when a request fails with model_not_supported, instead of surfacing the raw 400 error.

items.title: ECA 0.153.1
items.summary: Apply mcpTimeoutSeconds to MCP tools/prompts/resources listing, avoiding servers stuck in starting state when a list request never gets a response.
items.html: • Apply mcpTimeoutSeconds to MCP tools/prompts/resources listing, avoiding servers stuck in starting state when a list request never gets a response.

items.title: ECA 0.153.0
items.summary: Store chats in per-chat cache files with a lazy-loaded index instead of one whole-workspace blob, fixing CPU spikes and slow startup as history grows; legacy caches migrate automatically. #557 Hooks db_cache_path now points at the workspace cache dir instead…
items.html:
• Store chats in per-chat cache files with a lazy-loaded index instead of one whole-workspace blob, fixing CPU spikes and slow startup as history grows; legacy caches migrate automatically. #557

  • Hooks db_cache_path now points at the workspace cache dir instead of db.transit.json; read-chat --db-cache-path accepts the dir or a legacy file. #557

  • Keep compact_chat in the tool schema across normal and compact requests, preserving prompt-cache prefixes while rejecting calls outside active compaction.

  • Provide token metrics for ollama provider. #567.

items.title: ECA 0.152.0
items.summary: Share chat history across git worktrees of the same repo, and merge workspace cache writes from concurrent servers instead of overwriting. #558 Cache models.dev catalog on disk and fall back to it when the fetch fails, avoiding model capabilities silently…
items.html:
• Share chat history across git worktrees of the same repo, and merge workspace cache writes from concurrent servers instead of overwriting. #558
  • Cache models.dev catalog on disk and fall back to it when the fetch fails, avoiding model capabilities silently degrading (e.g. no image input) on transient network failures.
  • Fix ChatGPT OAuth routing and Responses Lite payloads for GPT-5.6 models. #563
  • Retry overloaded OpenAI post-tool requests without rerunning completed tools. #563

items.title: ECA 0.151.1
items.summary: Fix git tool heredoc failures for messages with apostrophes on old shells (e.g. macOS bash 3.2); git tool now honors toolCall.shellCommand path/args config. #562
items.html: • Fix git tool heredoc failures for messages with apostrophes on old shells (e.g. macOS bash 3.2); git tool now honors toolCall.shellCommand path/args config. #562

items.title: ECA 0.151.0
items.summary: Return exhausted provider errors and partial output from sub-agents instead of reporting successful empty results. Add provider retry config for retry counts, backoff, and chat recovery; no-output retries replay the original request. Fail fast with the…
items.html:
• Return exhausted provider errors and partial output from sub-agents instead of reporting successful empty results.
  • Add provider retry config for retry counts, backoff, and chat recovery; no-output retries replay the original request.
  • Fail fast with the resolved path when a hook action file doesn't exist; document that relative hook file paths resolve against the first workspace root.
  • Fix OpenAI Responses SSE errors, incomplete responses, and premature stream closes so chats retry or finish instead of staying active.
  • Return task status to LLM when changing. #556

items.title: ECA 0.150.1
items.summary: Add Claude Opus 5 support.
items.html: • Add Claude Opus 5 support.

items.title: ECA 0.150.0
items.summary: Abort in-flight LLM streaming requests promptly on prompt stop for OpenAI, GitHub Copilot, Google, Ollama and custom OpenAI-compatible providers (previously only Anthropic/Bedrock), including while waiting for the first token. #554 Don't reset a chat's model…
items.html:
• Abort in-flight LLM streaming requests promptly on prompt stop for OpenAI, GitHub Copilot, Google, Ollama and custom OpenAI-compatible providers (previously only Anthropic/Bedrock), including while waiting for the first token. #554

  • Don't reset a chat's model when changing the agent of an already started chat; the agent's defaultModel now only applies to chats without an established model. editor-code-assistant/eca-emacs#282

  • Fix plugin-provided agents missing from the editor's agent list when model sync finishes before plugin resolution (common with providers using fetchModels: false): re-emit the chat config after plugins resolve.

  • Surface Anthropic refusal stop reason (e.g. Fable safety classifiers) as a clear chat message with Anthropic's category/explanation instead of silently ending the prompt.

  • Improve @/# completion performance: enumerate files via git ls-files instead of walking the whole tree, cache dir candidates and avoid re-computing sort keys.

items.title: ECA 0.149.1
items.summary: Add text chat context type: inline client-supplied text (e.g. editor buffers, terminal output) with a label and content, delivered with the user message like images. Allows clients to send content that has no filesystem path.
items.html: • Add text chat context type: inline client-supplied text (e.g. editor buffers, terminal output) with a label and content, delivered with the user message like images. Allows clients to send content that has no filesystem path.

items.title: ECA 0.149.0
items.summary: Resolve plugin dependencies transitively: marketplace entries and .eca-plugin/plugin.json can declare plugins auto-loaded with the install. #552
items.html: • Resolve plugin dependencies transitively: marketplace entries and .eca-plugin/plugin.json can declare plugins auto-loaded with the install. #552

items.title: ECA 0.148.2
items.summary: Recover when the provider rejects an image in the request (e.g. xAI's 512px minimum on MCP tool images): retry without images instead of failing every subsequent prompt.
items.html: • Recover when the provider rejects an image in the request (e.g. xAI's 512px minimum on MCP tool images): retry without images instead of failing every subsequent prompt.

items.title: ECA 0.148.1
items.summary: Fix OpenRouter models failing every prompt with a context-window error: ignore catalog output limits >= context window and use limits from the provider's /models endpoint. Extend deepseek-v4 thinking variants (none, high, max) to also match deepseek-v4-flash…
items.html:
• Fix OpenRouter models failing every prompt with a context-window error: ignore catalog output limits >= context window and use limits from the provider's /models endpoint.
  • Extend deepseek-v4 thinking variants (none, high, max) to also match deepseek-v4-flash models.
  • Fix duplicate errors when a dead connection fails several stacked requests at once, which broke the auto-continue recovery and leaked state into the next prompt. #547

items.title: ECA 0.148.0
items.summary: Improve resilience to connections dropped by proxies/networks: retry stale pooled connections, classify the error clearly, auto-continue up to 3 times per prompt. #547 Fix streaming tool calls dropped when provider sends empty-string id in subsequent chunks…
items.html:
• Improve resilience to connections dropped by proxies/networks: retry stale pooled connections, classify the error clearly, auto-continue up to 3 times per prompt. #547
  • Fix streaming tool calls dropped when provider sends empty-string id in subsequent chunks (e.g. DashScope/Qwen Cloud).
  • Truncate oversized failed tool output, preserving full logs on disk instead of overflowing the model context.
  • Honor model output limits in OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Ollama requests while preserving extraPayload overrides.
  • Respect maxSteps in Markdown agent definitions.
  • Support variant in Markdown agent frontmatter.

items.title: OmniRush v3.7.3
items.summary: New The sandbox now sets itself up: on macOS the app starts its own small Linux VM (no Docker or other app needed), on Windows a Set up button installs WSL 2 with one admin prompt and resumes after the restart, and on Linux an Allow button does the one-time…
items.html:
New
  • The sandbox now sets itself up: on macOS the app starts its own small Linux VM (no Docker or other app needed), on Windows a Set up button installs WSL 2 with one admin prompt and resumes after the restart, and on Linux an Allow button does the one-time permission step. Progress and clear next steps show in the chat.
  • Servers you start in the sandbox open on this computer at the same localhost port.
Improved
  • Opening a project starts its sandbox right away, and the image downloads in the background, so the first message waits less.
  • In the sandbox, node_modules, Python environments and build folders are the sandbox's own Linux copies on macOS and Windows, so your Mac or Windows builds are never overwritten.
  • The agent carries multi-step tasks through to the end instead of stopping to ask whether to continue.
Fixed
  • Sandbox: a box with a fuse overlay no longer hangs on package installs, and starting a box never writes outside it.

items.title: OmniRush v3.7.2
items.summary: New Long chats have a Load earlier messages button at the top. Improved Computer use works on a display of its own with its own cursor, so your mouse, keyboard and clipboard stay yours. Fixed Undo and revert no longer remove chat turns or file changes without…
items.html:
New
  • Long chats have a Load earlier messages button at the top.
Improved
  • Computer use works on a display of its own with its own cursor, so your mouse, keyboard and clipboard stay yours.
Fixed
  • Undo and revert no longer remove chat turns or file changes without asking. Undo works only from the chat itself and ignores a held key, Revert and Edit say what they will take back, and hidden messages go only after you confirm a send.

items.title: OmniRush v3.7.1
items.summary: New See a command's output in the chat, while it runs and when it is done. How your allowance works: a help page for your daily tokens and the Good session checklist. Settings > General > Storage > Free up space removes files older versions left behind.…
items.html:
New
  • See a command's output in the chat, while it runs and when it is done.
  • How your allowance works: a help page for your daily tokens and the Good session checklist.
  • Settings > General > Storage > Free up space removes files older versions left behind.
Improved
  • Windows: after an update installs when you quit, the app opens again on the new version, and its shortcuts stay in place.
  • The built-in browser keeps working when you switch away, and asks for approval the way computer use does.
  • Clearer browser sign-in card: using your existing sign-ins is optional.
  • The window and the message box fit on short screens.
  • A shorter notice for settings not loaded from a project's config, and the chat title is no longer covered in the header.
  • The run status note shows only when something needs you (waiting for an answer, a message not yet confirmed, a retry), not during routine work.
Fixed
  • Computer use: "Allow for this chat" now applies to that one chat only, and a Deny withdraws the app's approval everywhere it was given.
  • Computer use from the terminal: copy the CLI connection again in the desktop app (its file was renamed).
  • Windows: messages that mention a local file send again.
  • Library: opening an item and going back works again (the page no longer gets stuck).
  • A chat saved with a model that is no longer available switches to the default OmniRush model and says so, instead of leaving Send disabled.

items.title: OmniRush v3.7.0
items.summary: Fixed The Mac app starts again. Desktop 3.6.7 and 3.6.9 stopped on macOS with "The bundled engine was changed". Also in this release (from 3.6.9) Security: commands the agent runs no longer receive the app's own keys. Security: approvals, permission mode,…
items.html:
Fixed
  • The Mac app starts again. Desktop 3.6.7 and 3.6.9 stopped on macOS with "The bundled engine was changed".
Also in this release (from 3.6.9)
  • Security: commands the agent runs no longer receive the app's own keys.
  • Security: approvals, permission mode, project settings, plugins, MCP servers and keys can only be changed from the app's own window, not with a key read from disk.
  • Computer use: no approval on each step; one Allow per app per chat. In Normal mode it still asks before paying or buying and before typing a password.

items.title: OmniRush v3.6.7
items.summary: Security A project's MCP settings can no longer hand the app's keys or files outside the project to an MCP server, and no local MCP server starts unless the app's checks are running. Better masking of access keys that tools print with escaped characters. New…
items.html:
Security
  • A project's MCP settings can no longer hand the app's keys or files outside the project to an MCP server, and no local MCP server starts unless the app's checks are running.
  • Better masking of access keys that tools print with escaped characters.
New
  • What's new: see what changed in each release from the sidebar, the Help menu or the command palette, and a short note after each update.
  • Themes: eight presets with light and dark versions, and your own theme in Settings › Appearance with a live preview and contrast checks. Share it as a code or a file; the editor, terminal and chat all follow it.
  • Computer use: the agent can operate an app window you approve (screenshots, clicks, typing), with a stop control and approvals that follow your permission mode. Off until it is enabled for your account.
  • Editor: search, problems and language features, a split editor, editor settings, Markdown and image preview, and a Git change gutter. Format on save asks once before running a project's own formatter.
Improved
  • Only OmniRush models are offered. Other providers, and your own opencode plugins and custom tools, stay off.
  • Fewer repeated failed edits: when an edit can't find its text, the agent now sees the file's current lines.
  • The reasoning effort shown in the model picker is always the one used.
  • The session quality status now sits inside its chip instead of above the chat.

items.title: OmniRush v3.6.3
items.summary: Security A project's own plugins, language servers and formatters are no longer loaded from its configuration. MCP servers start through the system's own npx and uvx, never a copy inside the project. Added Permission modes: Careful asks before every file…
items.html:
Security

  • A project's own plugins, language servers and formatters are no longer loaded from its configuration.
  • MCP servers start through the system's own npx and uvx, never a copy inside the project.

Added

  • Permission modes: Careful asks before every file change and command, Normal (the default) asks only before risky actions, Auto never asks.
  • A notification when a task finishes or waits for your approval.
  • Chat and IDE layouts.
  • Figma designs through a supported MCP server.

Fixed

  • Session sharing is turned off; it used an outside service that has shut down.
  • A calmer start screen: the greeting and the composer, with your recent chats in one line below it.
  • Long answers are kept in sync while they run.
  • The handoff question is asked once per chat, only when the chat is idle; a failed handoff can be retried.
  • Undo keeps your editor saves and refreshes open files.
  • Skills you added are kept when you update.
  • The approval buttons fit in a narrow chat.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/omnirush-ai/omnirush-gui/compare/v3.6.2...v3.6.3

items.title: OmniRush v3.6.2
items.summary: Security MCP servers defined in a project's own configuration no longer start on their own. Only supported servers start, at a supported version, working inside the project; others are listed with the reason they were skipped. Added A code editor beside the…
items.html:
Security

  • MCP servers defined in a project's own configuration no longer start on their own. Only supported servers start, at a supported version, working inside the project; others are listed with the reason they were skipped.

Added

  • A code editor beside the chat.
  • Review your changes and fix what the review found; undo the last turn while keeping your own later edits, and redo it; see the chat's changes and status.
  • Parallel tasks, each in its own copy of the project, and a home screen with recent projects and chats and a search of past chats.
  • The agent checks its own changes with the project's checks, keeps project notes in AGENTS.md, sees code diagnostics after edits, and writes fuller summaries when a long chat is compacted. Each can be switched off in Settings.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/omnirush-ai/omnirush-gui/compare/v3.6.1...v3.6.2

items.html:
OmniRush.ai 3.4.4

  • Clearer Linux sandbox setup: a simple card per project with live download progress, an Advanced section for the backend, and one clear next step for your OS when a sandbox runtime is missing.

  • Bigger projects count: project copies now go up to 2 GiB (was 256 MiB), with a free-space check so a small disk never fills up.
  • Every project-copy decision now has a plain reason, and a short tip after a turn suggests a follow-up.
  • Faster sandbox start, and sandboxes from other users or re-cloned folders are handled cleanly.

items.title: OmniRush v3.4.0
items.summary: What's new An optional Linux sandbox for each project. Turn it on for a project, and the agent's commands run in a Linux sandbox kept for that project, while the app, your chats and your files stay on your computer. Packages installed in the sandbox are still…
items.html:
What's new

  • An optional Linux sandbox for each project. Turn it on for a project, and the agent's commands run in a Linux sandbox kept for that project, while the app, your chats and your files stay on your computer. Packages installed in the sandbox are still there next time.
  • The best sandbox tool on each computer. Linux: bubblewrap, Podman or Docker. macOS: OrbStack, colima, Docker Desktop, Rancher Desktop or Podman, with Apple's container when you choose it. Windows: WSL containers, the OmniRush WSL distro, Docker Desktop or Podman. Settings shows which one is used and why, and lets you pick your own.
  • Same versions, every time. Package installs the agent runs (npm, pip, cargo, apt and more) go through light wrappers in the agent's own shell, so a project can be set up again with the same versions. Your own terminal is never changed.

Fixes

  • Files that background commands finish writing after a turn ends are picked up before your next message.
  • Reopened chats keep counting their turns from where they left off.
  • Very large turns, such as ones that install many packages, are kept whole.
  • Fewer routine notifications, and quieter voice recording.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/omnirush-ai/omnirush-gui/compare/v3.3.7...v3.4.0

items.html:
中秋限时限定版

PI-Desktop 0.15.7 正式版，特别加入中秋限时体验：首次启动播放全屏月下动画，也可在设置中再次播放。

Highlights

  • 可选本地语音输入，支持可取消且带校验的模型下载，并保护过期转写结果。
  • Windows Portable 单文件版本与安装包、ZIP 一同发布。
  • 改进 Agent 取消/恢复、模型与 Provider 处理、批量图片和工作面板体验。

This is the official 0.15.7 Mid-Autumn limited-time edition.

完整变更记录： https://github.com/vastsa/PI-Desktop/compare/v0.15.6...v0.15.7

items.html:
🪿 Goose v1.30.0 Release Notes

Released: April 8, 2026

✨ New Features

🖥️ Terminal UI (TUI) Overhaul
  • Tab-expandable tool calls — tool call output now collapses cleanly with tab to expand (#8136)
  • Improved message rendering — better ordering, streaming/scrolling, and overall visual polish for messages, tool calls, and text entry (#8144, #8156, #8214)
  • Independent --text mode — text mode is now decoupled from the normal TUI for a cleaner headless experience (#8210)
  • goose serve — new subcommand to run Goose as a background service (#8209)
🔌 Providers & Models
  • Gemini OAuth provider — first-class OAuth-based authentication for Google Gemini (#8129)
  • Copilot ACP provider — new provider for GitHub Copilot via ACP (#8154)
  • Zhipu declarative provider — adds Zhipu AI with configurable ZHIPU_BASE_URL override (#8204)
  • Configurable fast_model for declarative providers — lets you specify a lightweight model for quick tasks (#8194)
  • Gemma 4 local model support — enable Gemma 4 as a local model option (#8366)
  • VMware Tanzu Platform provider improvements — bug fixes, streaming support, and UI enhancements (#8126)
🛡️ Security & Observability
  • Egress logging inspector — new security feature to log and inspect outbound network calls (#8149)
  • Restricted secrets file permissions — secrets files are now created with tighter OS-level permissions (#8118)
🧩 Extensions & Skills
  • Show installed skills in UI — skills are now visible and browsable from the desktop app (#7910)
  • Skills platform extension — skills are now managed as a dedicated platform extension (#8377)
  • Recursively discover nested skills — skills under configured roots are now found at any depth (#8082)
  • Configurable extension timeouts — set timeouts per-extension via ACP _meta or a global default (#8295)
  • Reusable ACP provider controls — shared UI components for ACP provider configuration (#8314)
  • Rust ACP client for extension methods (#8227)
  • Developer MCP server enhancements (#7770)
🌐 Internationalization
  • i18n infrastructure — added react-intl based internationalization framework to the desktop app (#8105)
🩺 Diagnostics
  • goose doctor — new command to diagnose common configuration and environment issues (#8342)
⚙️ Configuration
  • GOOSE_SHOW_FULL_OUTPUT — new config option to disable tool output truncation (#7919)
  • GOOSE_CLI_SHOW_THINKING — can now be set in config.yaml (not just env vars) (#8097)
  • GOOSE_CONTEXT_LIMIT — now readable from config.yaml (#7900)
  • GOOSE_DISABLE_KEYRING — now honoured from config.yaml at startup (#8219)
  • Per-delegate max_turns override (#8066)
  • skip_canonical_filtering for declarative providers (#8052)
🏗️ Build & Packaging
  • Optional native-tls support — alternative to rustls for environments that need system TLS (#8037)
  • Feature-gated AWS provider dependencies — behind aws-providers feature flag for leaner builds (#8080)
  • Feature-gated telemetry — telemetry is now behind Cargo feature flags (#8119)
  • Inference Mesh settings tab (#8094)

🐛 Bug Fixes

Providers
  • Fix user message text silently dropped when message contains both text and image (#8071)
  • Send empty object instead of null for Bedrock tool input (#8121)
  • Fall back to configured models when the models endpoint fetch fails (#7530)
  • Prevent Ollama provider from hanging on tool-calling requests (#7723)
  • Increase Ollama retry config + add transient-only retry mode (#7677)
  • Use safely_parse_json for OpenAI streaming tool arguments (#8208)
  • Use v1beta1 API version for Google/MaaS models on GCP Vertex AI (#8278)
  • Use build_host_url for GCP Vertex AI location fallback (#8185)

items.html:
本版新增用量页“今日”小时视图和 Patina 主题，辅助会话支持 Markdown 与流式进度，改过文件的回合不再默认被追问检查，并修复多处内存、卡住和显示问题。

新增

  • 内置 Patina 主题，雾灰画布、白色浮卡与钢蓝强调色，明暗两套，需要时在设置里手动选择。关联 #14136 by @FuchaZ。
  • 用量页多了“今日”范围，单日窗口按小时显示用量、花费和请求。关联 #14176 by @EMEEEEMMMM。

变更

  • 改过文件的回合不再默认被要求先做检查、复核和签收才能结束；需要时在用户配置里设 host_verification = "on"。"交付"预设和 --fail-on-unverified 仍会要求。关联 #14154。
  • 隐藏图标栏时，侧栏不再有两个打开同一个“远程”设置页的入口；底部重复的“连接与机器”已移除，顶部“运行环境”仍可进入。关联 #14187。
  • 自动命名遇到关不掉思考的模型时，会明确提示“模型把输出额度花在思考上”，并建议换一个能关闭思考的命名模型。关联 #14188。
  • 隐藏图标栏时，侧栏搜索行与下面的快捷入口之间不再有多余空白；两处小字提示统一使用“·”分隔。关联 #14191。

修复

  • 配置了 TCP 方式的 DNS 服务器时，健康探测把正常应答的服务器误判为不可用，导致第一个服务器失效后不会切换到下一个。关联 #14044 by @imcreazy。
  • 只打开了远程会话窗格时，直接访问本机端口（不带窗格前缀）的请求没有应答，现在会转发给远端内核；本地窗格仍然优先。关联 #14045 by @imcreazy。
  • 注入的常驻上下文（技能清单、项目指令、规则、日期）不再因为「已交付」的书签而漏发。关联 #14099 by @chuiwenwei。
  • 扩展拒绝、取消、折叠、回退、截断之后，都会按模型真正看到的历史重新判断。关联 #14099 by @chuiwenwei。
  • 服务端新建会话（/new）的首个请求现在会带上技能清单、项目指令与日期。关联 #14099 by @chuiwenwei。
  • 用量页与 hero 的「实付」现在包含守护评审这些安全审查的花费（此前它们的 token 计入而钱没计入）。关联 #14110 by @chuiwenwei。
  • 用量总额现在把"只计了次数和 token、没有金额"的调用（旧版本写入的记录、标题生成）算作未定价，总额标成下限而不是账单。关联 #14112 by @chuiwenwei。
  • 标题生成的调用现在会按价目计价，不再只计 token 不计钱。关联 #14112 by @chuiwenwei。
  • 旧版 1.x 历史索引不再保留已回退或被覆盖的消息正文，降低启动时的内存压力。关联 #14116。
  • browser_act 的脚本等待一个永远不会结束的 Promise 时不再无限期卡住（有用户等了十分钟以上）；30 秒后停止脚本，并告诉模型"脚本超时"。关联 #14118 fixed in #14143。
  • 最终回答后的工作区观察遇到阻塞 I/O 时，会话不再长时间显示运行中；停止操作会取消观察和证据封存的等待，未完成的观察记录为证据缺口。关联 #13953、#14140 by @SivanCola。
  • 上下文压缩超时或取消时，不再因摘要流同时关闭而误报成功或采用未完成的摘要。关联 #14144 by @SivanCola。
  • 从微信等应用复制文件粘贴到输入框时，文件会先复制成附件再发送，不再登记原路径，避免来源应用的缓存路径读不到而失败。关联 #14150 by @KHG420。
  • 辅助会话面板里的回答现在按 Markdown 显示，加粗、行内代码和列表不再露出原始符号。关联 #14157。
  • 辅助问题立即显示提问，流式显示回答文字、阶段和耗时；中断的回答标为未完成，输入保留可重试。关联 #14162 by @lancy69。
  • 输入 /mcp、/skills 时，补全只提供真正会执行的子命令；输入不认识的子命令会明确提示，而不是悄悄显示列表。关联 #14167。
  • 宿主发出的「本轮还有未完成事项」的续做提示不再被当成你发的话，不会再变成会话标题、预览或用户轮次。关联 #14170 by @imcreazy。
  • 设置里“模型可用的工具”不再显示英文原文；内置工具按界面语言给出一句话说明，被截断的说明也不再在词中间断开。关联 #14175。
  • 隐藏图标栏时，侧栏底部的“连接与机器”不再比其他入口更大更粗，和同类入口使用同一字号和字重。关联 #14184。

升级须知

  • 没有价目的行不再显示成 ¥0，而是把总额标为「未定价调用未计入」的下限。关联 #14110 by @chuiwenwei。
  • 超过 64 MiB 安全预算的记录、有效消息正文或 DAG 元数据会被拒绝；原文件保持不变，其他会话仍可索引。关联 #14116。
  • 没设过这一项的用户升级后，回合收尾前不再被追问"还欠什么"；项目配置文件仍改不了这一项。关联 #14154。

贡献者

感谢本版本的贡献者：@FuchaZ、@EMEEEEMMMM、@imcreazy、@chuiwenwei、@SivanCola、@KHG420、@lancy69

This release adds an hourly Today view to Usage and a Patina theme, renders side-conversation answers as Markdown with streamed progress, stops asking for checks by default after a turn that changed files, and fixes several memory, hang and display problems.

New

  • A built-in Patina theme with a grey canvas, white cards and a steel-blue accent, in light and dark, chosen in Settings when you want it. Refs #14136 by @FuchaZ.
  • The Usage page has a Today range, and any one-day window shows usage, spend and requests by the hour. Refs #14176 by @EMEEEEMMMM.

Changed

  • A turn that changed files is no longer held open until a check, review and sign-off exist; set host_verification = "on" in your user config for that. Refs #14154.
  • With the icon rail hidden, the sidebar no longer has two entries to the same Remote settings page; the duplicate bottom row is gone and "Environments" still opens it. Refs #14187.
  • When a model that cannot turn thinking off spends its budget thinking, automatic naming now says so and suggests a naming model that can. Refs #14188.
  • With the icon rail hidden, the blank band between the sidebar's search row and the shortcut rows is gone, and both hints use the same "·" separator. Refs #14191.

Fixed

  • The DNS server health probe read a TCP reply as if it had no length prefix and reported a live server as dead, so failover to the next [network] server never happened. Refs #14044 by @imcreazy.
  • A request made straight to the port with no pane prefix got no answer while only a remote pane was open; it now goes to the far kernel, and a local pane still takes precedence. Refs #14045 by @imcreazy.
  • Injected standing context (skills listing, project instructions, rules, the date) can no longer be believed delivered when the model never got it. Refs #14099 by @chuiwenwei.
  • A refusal, cancel, fold, rewind or truncation now re-asks the model-visible history instead of a bookmark. Refs #14099 by @chuiwenwei.
  • A new session in the served app now starts with the skills listing, project instructions and the date. Refs #14099 by @chuiwenwei.
  • The usage page and hero paid total now include the guardian's safety reviews, whose tokens were counted but whose money was not. Refs #14110 by @chuiwenwei.
  • The usage total now treats a call that was counted but carries no amount (pre-schema rows, title generation) as unpriced, so the total is a floor rather than a bill. Refs #14112 by @chuiwenwei.
  • Title-generation calls are now priced from the rate card instead of counting tokens with no money. Refs #14112 by @chuiwenwei.
  • Legacy 1.x indexing retains payload locations, not discarded message bodies. Preflight no longer copies large strings. Refs #14116.
  • A browser_act script awaiting a promise that never settles no longer holds the call forever; after 30 seconds it is stopped and the model is told it timed out. Refs #14118 fixed in #14143.
  • Blocked workspace observation no longer holds a turn after its final answer; Stop cancels observation and seal waits, and incomplete observations remain gaps. Refs #13953, #14140 by @SivanCola.
  • Context compaction no longer reports success or accepts an unfinished digest when its summary stream closes at the same time as a timeout or cancellation. Refs #14144 by @SivanCola.
  • A file pasted from another application, such as WeChat, is now copied into an attachment instead of being registered by its original path, which could fail to read later. Refs #14150 by @KHG420.
  • Answers in the side conversation panel are now drawn as Markdown, so bold, inline code and lists no longer show raw markers. Refs #14157.
  • Side questions show your question immediately and stream the answer, phase and elapsed time; interrupted answers are marked incomplete and drafts stay available for retry. Refs #14162 by @lancy69.
  • /mcp and /skills completion now offers only the subcommands that run, and an unrecognised one is reported instead of silently printing the listing. Refs #14167.
  • The host's own "work still outstanding" prompt is no longer read back as something you typed, so it stops becoming a session title, a preview line or a user turn. Refs #14170 by @imcreazy.
  • The tool list in Settings no longer shows the model-facing English text; built-in tools get a one-line description in the interface language, and a long line is cut cleanly. Refs #14175.
  • With the icon rail hidden, the sidebar's "Connections & machines" row is no longer larger and bolder than the other shortcut rows; they share one size and weight. Refs #14184.

Upgrade notes

  • A row with no price no longer shows as zero; the total is marked as a floor with "unpriced calls not included". Refs #14110 by @chuiwenwei.
  • Records, retained payloads, and DAG metadata have separate 64 MiB budgets. Refusals preserve files, never use stale checkpoints, and leave healthy sources indexable. Refs #14116.
  • If you never set this key, the end-of-turn "still owes" prompts stop after upgrading; a project config cannot change it. Refs #14154.

Contributors

Thanks to this release's contributors: @FuchaZ, @EMEEEEMMMM, @imcreazy, @chuiwenwei, @SivanCola, @KHG420, @lancy69

What's Changed

  • fix(browser): stop an eval script whose promise never settles by @esengine in https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/pull/14143
  • fix(agent): reject interrupted summaries at EOF / 修复压缩流结束与取消竞态 by @SivanCola in https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/pull/14144
  • fix(stats): quote a guardian review's usage like any other call by @chuiwenwei in https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/pull/14110
  • fix(control): derive projection delivery from the visible history by @chuiwenwei in https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/pull/14099
